t: What stands here is the tower of St Mary Somerset, on Upper Thames Street. It is all that remains of a church first recorded in the twelfth century. The Great Fire of 1666 destroyed that church, and it was rebuilt by the office of Sir Christopher Wren, one of 51 City churches rebuilt that way. Wren is named as its designer. He is the architect who also gave London St Paul's Cathedral. The body of the church was demolished in 1871, leaving the tower standing on its own.
